mn150:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, and he arrived at a village of the Kosalan brahmin householders named Nagaravinda.
mn150:2.1: The brahmin householders of Nagaravinda heard:
mn150:2.2: ‘The ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from a Sakyan clan, wandering in the Kosalan country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, has arrived at Nagaravinda.
mn150:2.3: Now a good report of that Master Gotama has been spread about thus:
mn150:2.4: “That Blessed One is such since he is accomplished, fully enlightened, perfect in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of worlds, incomparable leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed.”
mn150:2.5: He describes this world with its gods, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its gods and humans, which he has himself realized through direct knowledge.
mn150:2.6: He teaches a Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he proclaims the holy life that is utterly perfect and pure.
mn150:2.7: It is good to see such arahants.’
mn150:3.1: Then the brahmin householders of Nagaravinda went to the Blessed One; some of them, having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down at one side; some exchanged greetings with him, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, sat down at one side; some raised their hands palms together in salutation to the Blessed One and sat down at one side; some pronounced their name and clan in the Blessed One’s presence and sat down at one side; some kept silent and sat down at one side. When the brahmin householders of Nagaravinda were seated at one side, the Blessed One said this to them:
mn150:4.1: ‘Householders, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you thus:
mn150:4.2: “Householders, what sort of ascetics and brahmins should not be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated?”—
mn150:4.3: being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus:
mn150:4.4: “Those ascetics and brahmins who are not rid of lust, not rid of hate, not rid of delusion regarding forms cognizable by the eye, whose minds are not stilled within, and who conduct themselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind—such ascetics and brahmins should not be honoured, respected, revered, or venerated.
mn150:4.6: Because we too are not rid of lust, not rid of hate, not rid of delusion regarding forms cognizable by the eye, our minds are not stilled within, and we conduct ourselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind; since we see no higher conduct than our own in these good ascetics and brahmins,
mn150:4.7: therefore those ascetics and brahmins should not be honoured, respected, revered, or venerated.
mn150:4.8: Those ascetics and brahmins who are not rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn150:4.9: regarding odours cognizable by the nose …
mn150:4.10: regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn150:4.11: regarding tangibles cognizable by the body …
mn150:4.12: who are not rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding dhammas cognizable by the mind, whose minds are not stilled within, and who conduct themselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind—such ascetics and brahmins should not be honoured, respected, revered, or venerated.
mn150:4.14: Because we too are not rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding dhammas cognizable by the mind, our minds are not stilled within, and we conduct ourselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind; since we see no higher conduct than our own in these good ascetics and brahmins,
mn150:4.15: therefore those ascetics and brahmins should not be honoured, respected, revered, or venerated.”
mn150:4.16: Being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus.
mn150:5.1: But, householders, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you thus:
mn150:5.2: “Householders, what sort of ascetics and brahmins should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated?”—
mn150:5.3: being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus:
mn150:5.4: “Those ascetics and brahmins who are rid of lust, rid of hate, rid of delusion regarding forms cognizable by the eye, whose minds are stilled within, and who conduct themselves rightly in body, speech, and mind—such ascetics and brahmins should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.
mn150:5.6: Because we are not rid of lust, not rid of hate, not rid of delusion regarding forms cognizable by the eye, our minds are not stilled within, and we conduct ourselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind; since we see a higher conduct than our own in these good ascetics and brahmins,
mn150:5.7: therefore those ascetics and brahmins should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.
mn150:5.8: Those ascetics and brahmins who are rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn150:5.9: regarding odours cognizable by the nose …
mn150:5.10: regarding flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn150:5.11: regarding tangibles cognizable by the body …
mn150:5.12: who are rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding dhammas cognizable by the mind, whose minds are stilled within, and who conduct themselves rightly in body, speech, and mind—such ascetics and brahmins should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.
mn150:5.14: Because we are not rid of lust, hate, and delusion regarding dhammas cognizable by the mind, our minds are not stilled within, and we conduct ourselves sometimes rightly and sometimes wrongly in body, speech, and mind; since we see a higher conduct than our own in these good ascetics and brahmins,
mn150:5.15: therefore those ascetics and brahmins should be honoured, respected, revered, and venerated.”
mn150:5.16: Being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus.
mn150:6.1: But, householders, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you thus:
mn150:6.2: “But what is the reason, what is the ground, venerable ones, by which you speak thus?
mn150:6.3: Surely those venerable ones are either rid of lust or have entered on the way to remove lust; are either rid of hate or have entered on the way to remove hate; are either rid of delusion or have entered on the way to remove delusion”—
mn150:6.4: being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus:
mn150:6.5: “Indeed, those venerable ones resort to remote jungle-thicket resting places in the forest.
mn150:6.6: There there are no such forms cognizable by the eye that, having seen them again and again, they would delight in; there are no such sounds cognizable by the ear that, having heard them again and again, they would delight in; there are no such odours cognizable by the nose that, having smelled them again and again, they would delight in; there are no such flavours cognizable by the tongue that, having tasted them again and again, they would delight in; there are no such tangibles cognizable by the body that, having touched them again and again, they would delight in.
mn150:6.7: These, friends, are the reason, this is the ground, by which we speak thus—
mn150:6.8: surely those venerable ones are either rid of lust or have entered on the way to remove lust; are either rid of hate or have entered on the way to remove hate; are either rid of delusion or have entered on the way to remove delusion.”
mn150:6.9: Being asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus.’
mn150:7.1: When this was said, the brahmin householders of Nagaravinda said to the Blessed One:
mn150:7.3: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama, as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyes to see forms.
mn150:7.4: We go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
mn150:7.5: From today let Master Gotama accept us as lay followers who have gone to him for refuge for life.’
mn150:7.6: The Discourse to the Nagaravindans, the eighth, is finished.
